driveway.label: Driveway
driveway.title: A clearer arrival, after dark.
driveway.intro: Guide the approach to homes and small premises. Start with the driveway width, wall position and sensor response — then select the product format.
driveway.caption: A considered welcome. A visible approach.
driveway.sub: Motion-sensor lighting for arrival points and the way home.
driveway.heading: Light the approach.
checks: Direct adjustable heads toward the approach
Keep the solar panel clear of overhangs
Match sensor behavior to people and vehicles
questions: Understand the approach
Share the driveway width, mounting position and approach direction. A site photo makes the brief easier to assess.
Plan for usable sunlight
An exposed mounting point may suit an integrated unit. A shaded wall may call for a separate panel.
Agree on operating behavior
Specify motion-only, dim-to-bright or other required modes. Runtime must be assessed against the final configuration.

entryway.label: Entryway
entryway.title: Make every entrance feel considered.
entryway.intro: Bring light to doors, gates and side entrances. Choose a compact wall format or a separate panel for installations beneath an overhang.
entryway.caption: A brighter welcome starts at the door.
entryway.sub: Wall-mounted lighting for entrances and everyday access.
entryway.heading: Make the first step clear.
checks: Map the doorway, gate and approach path
Consider shade from porches and roof edges
Confirm sensor coverage before sample approval
questions: Define the access point
A single door, a wider gateway and a side passage need different light distribution. Start with a photo and approximate dimensions.
Check the mounting surface
Confirm masonry, cladding or another surface. Include mounting hardware requirements in the quotation request.
Protect the user experience
Describe the desired trigger behavior and light color. Confirm these with a sample before a larger order.

perimeter.label: Perimeter
perimeter.title: Bring clarity to the boundary.
perimeter.intro: Boundary walls and side passages need a planned sequence of light. Combine mounting positions, daytime exposure and operating requirements in one project brief.
perimeter.caption: Consider the whole route.
perimeter.sub: A project begins with the space, the mounting points and the night-time need.
perimeter.heading: Think beyond one fixture.
checks: Mark each mounting point on a simple plan
Ask for coverage and runtime evidence
questions: Mark the complete route
Share the boundary length, obstructions and likely mounting points. This helps identify where different formats may be needed.
Separate light and panel needs
A mounting point with poor daylight may benefit from a split format. Plan cable routes before selecting a final model.
Define the coverage target
Agree on light distribution and operating hours. Request a lighting calculation where the project requires it.

garden.label: Garden & path
garden.title: Let the landscape lead the way.
garden.intro: Add accent lighting around planting and paths. Build a coordinated outdoor assortment while keeping landscape lighting and security lighting requirements distinct.
garden.caption: Small details. A more inviting garden.
garden.sub: Solar spotlights for planting, edges and outdoor features.
garden.heading: Build a complete outdoor range.
checks: Separate accent light from security coverage
Choose daylight access over hidden placement
Coordinate the light color across the range
questions: Identify the focal points
List planting, pathways and architectural features. Decide whether the priority is atmosphere, guidance or security.
Allow for seasonal growth
Consider shade from growing plants and trees. Keep panel exposure in the brief, including the installation season.
Plan the range as a whole
Decide pack sizes and complementary wall-light families. Retail-ready packaging can be part of the same inquiry.
